newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold ends down on platinum, post-OTC sales.
newsitem.headline: HK gold ends down on platinum, post-OTC sales.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended lower on Tuesday compared to its previous New York close, pressured by platinum and leftover selling from the options expiry with no good news to provide support, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$339.00/50 an ounce against New York's US$339.30/80 close on Monday.
Dealers said that pressure on platinum was spilling over to the gold market.
Some traders reported leftover sales from Monday's over-the-counter (OTC) options expiry.
"There is nothing in particular, just bad news still hanging over the market," a senior dealer said.
Reports that the Swiss may drop opposition to International Monetary Fund gold sales were only contributing to the already bearish sentiment that marked gold, dealers said.
Resistance was now seen at $340 per ounce while initial support was $338. If gold breached that, the next support level was $336, traders said.
"Physical demand has increased a little bit," said one trader.
Local gold ended HK$18 lower at HK$3,141 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -1.00 from its previous fix at -5.00
